channel.title: mint - news
channel.description: Get the latest news and analysis on business, finance, politics from mint, the website of the Mint newspaper, one of India's leading business and financial dailies

item.title: Trump sued over White House media ban; 6 citizens claim public’s right to know is at stake
item.description: The lawsuit argues that restricting access for news organisations over their coverage deprives the public of independent reporting about the president and his administration.

item.title: A pause before escalation? Why Iran fears a all-out war after US midterm polls as Donald Trump weighs his next move
item.description: Iranians are bracing for a possible return to full-scale war as Trump bolsters US military forces in the Middle East. With economic pressure mounting and Iran warning of retaliation, fears are growing that hostilities could resume after the US midterm elections.

item.title: LTCG news: Budget 2027-28 may cut long-term capital gains tax for both domestic and foreign investors, says report
item.description: Government weighs lowering 12.5% capital gains levy, allowing foreign investors to calculate gains in dollar terms

item.title: Europe is adding to businesses' regulatory burden, says Piyush Goyal
item.description: At a business forum in The Hague, commerce minister said&nbsp;India is a trusted nation that doesn't steal data, technology, and ideas.

item.title: Rahul Gandhi convoy accident: What led to vehicles colliding on Purvanchal Expressway? UP Police SIT to begin probe
item.description: Uttar Pradesh Police has formed an SIT to investigate the collision involving vehicles in Rahul Gandhi’s convoy on the Purvanchal Expressway. The probe will examine the cause of the pile-up, security arrangements and traffic coordination. Gandhi was safe, and his convoy continued to Sultanpur.

item.title: SIR controversy: Election Commission says all three members approved orders, denies amending Form 6
item.description: In its counter-affidavit filed before the apex court, the poll panel said the SIR orders issued on June 24, 2025, October 27, 2025, and May 14, 2026, were approved unanimously by Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar and Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi.

item.title: Nepal gets $20 mn in UN aid after $2.7 bn flood losses: Is climate finance failing vulnerable nations?
item.description: Nepal will receive $20 million from the UN’s loss and damage fund after August floods killed around 1,500 people and caused $2.7 billion in infrastructure losses. With reconstruction costs topping $4.7 billion, the aid highlights the gap between climate finance and vulnerable nations’ needs.

item.title: From coding to cultivation? AI job fears prompt software engineer to consider farming as an alternative career
item.description: A software engineer with nearly a decade of experience has sparked a Reddit debate after saying rapid advances in artificial intelligence have made him consider farming or growing his own food. His post highlights concerns about how AI could reshape software development and the future of work.

item.title: Israel elections 2026: What happens if no party can secure a 61-seat Knesset majority? Top scenarios explained
item.description: Israel’s 2026 elections: With 61 of 120 seats needed for a majority, parties could explore alliances, a unity government, minority rule or fresh elections if negotiations fail.

item.title: India, US fine-tuning trade deal after concluding most discussions, says minister Piyush Goyal
item.description: The proposed trade agreement could give Indian exporters greater certainty on US tariffs as New Delhi pursues preferential access to economies accounting for a majority of global GDP.

item.title: Why Siang project matters for India as China builds mega Brahmaputra dam, and why Arunachal locals are up in arms
item.description: India’s proposed 11,200-MW Siang dam in Arunachal Pradesh aims to boost water storage and manage flood risks amid China’s upstream mega-dam plans. But protests highlight local fears over displacement, ancestral land, environmental damage and inadequate consultation.

item.title: Govt clears ₹2.12 lakh crore defence procurements, including kamikaze drones and helicopters
item.description: The procurement proposals were approved by the Defence Acquisition Council (DAC), the defence ministry's highest decision-making body on military procurement. It was chaired by Defence Minister Rajnath Singh.

item.title: California election controversy explained: Why the Department of Justice and state are squaring off over voter rolls
item.description: The Justice Department sued California over more than 20,000 people it suspects are noncitizens on voter rolls, seeking verification before related ballots are counted. California disputes the federal list’s accuracy and says the late intervention could disenfranchise eligible voters.&nbsp;

item.title: After 30 yrs in UAE, Indian expat in Sharjah wins 12.9 cr in UAE Lottery: 'Now I have a chance to apply for Golden Visa'
item.description: Kishore Pandurang Rao bought the winning ticket for AED 50 (around ₹1,300) on the UAE Lottery platform. He used the Easy Pick option, which automatically selected the numbers for him. Matching all six numbers in the ‘days’ section earned him the AED 5 million prize.

item.title: Brazil election 2026 results: What’s the net worth of Lula Da Silva as he gets re-elected as president for fourth term?
item.description: Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva declared assets worth R$4.78 million, about $953,000, in his 2026 filing. That is 35.7% below his 2022 declaration. Private pension plans account for nearly 69% of his reported assets; declared values do not necessarily reflect current market value.

item.title: Who is Anbil Mahesh Poyyamozhi? Meet the former Tamil Nadu minister arrested in ₹100 crore school scam case
item.description: Anbil Mahesh Poyyamozhi is a DMK leader from Tiruchirappalli, Tamil Nadu, and a close associate of DMK youth wing secretary Udhayanidhi Stalin. He served as the state's school education minister after the DMK formed the government in 2021.

item.title: Income Tax department nudges taxpayers to disclose overseas properties
item.description: Under the one-time FAST-DS scheme, eligible taxpayers can disclose specified foreign assets by 31 December, with tax and penalty relief for qualifying declarations.

item.title: Namo Yamuna River Safari: When will Delhi’s 5-km cruise start? Location, ticket price, nearest Delhi metro station
item.description: The project, being developed between Sonia Vihar and Jagatpur, will begin trial operations on Monday.

item.title: Saudi King approves 500 Saudi riyals monthly allowance (approx ₹12,000) ahead of utility tariff changes: Who gets it?
item.description: The royal directives cover both direct financial assistance to eligible households and measures intended to improve wages and employment conditions for Saudi nationals.

item.title: India’s green hydrogen ambition is going global; 14 deals in just the first four months of 2026, says Amitabh Kant
item.description: India signed 14 binding clean hydrogen supply contracts in the first four months of 2026, covering 311,520 metric tonnes of annual supply, with 62% destined for export markets, former NITI Aayog CEO Amitabh Kant said. The contracts signal India's growing ambitions in the global clean energy trade.

item.title: ‘Saddam Hussein opened a Cheesecake Factory’: Obama’s savage takedown of Trump’s White House makeover — what he said
item.description: Taking aim at the president’s aesthetic choices, Obama told the crowd: “He’s got the White House looking like Saddam Hussein opened a Cheesecake Factory.”

item.title: Mumbai local train services hit by hanging OHE wire; Central Railway's mainline disrupted
item.description: Hanging OHE wire disrupts Mumbai local train services; office-goers face delays

item.title: ‘Make a deal’ or ‘finish it off’: Trump warns ‘decision time’ nears on Iran amid threat of fresh strikes
item.description: Trump has asked Iran to strike a deal or face renewed military action, calling it “decision time” for Tehran. As tensions over the Strait of Hormuz escalate, Iran has denied offering to reopen the key shipping route in exchange for the lifting of the US naval blockade.

item.title: China's $168 billion Brahmaputra dam faces fresh concerns as researchers warn of rising flood risks
item.description: Chinese researchers warn that rising runoff in Tibet’s Yarlung Tsangpo, which flows into India as the Brahmaputra, could heighten flood risks this century. The findings raise fresh concerns as China builds its $168 billion mega hydropower project.

item.title: Namo Ghat helipad security breach: UP man poses as fake Army officer during Varanasi air show, arrested
item.description: Police became vigilant after receiving information about a suspicious individual, prompting them to question him.

item.title: Storm Boelo weather warnings: UK faces strong winds, heavy rain and travel disruption as second storm hits
item.description: Storm Boelo brought strong winds and heavy rain to Scotland, Northern Ireland, and northern England, disrupting transport and causing power cuts. The storm followed Storm Austen. Authorities have warned the public about flooding, dangerous coastal conditions, and fallen trees.

item.title: Celebrations begin after Serbia elections 2026 results | Explained - How historic students movement brought down Vučić
item.description: After 14 years of Vucic's political dominance, Serbia faces a new phase in its political development. Whether the student-backed movement can turn its electoral mandate into lasting institutional change will depend on how it organises its leadership.

item.title: Cyclone Arnab latest updates: Andhra Pradesh landfall likely on October 28; Odisha shuts schools in 6 districts
item.description: Cyclone Arnab is expected to intensify into a severe cyclonic storm before making landfall along the Andhra Pradesh coast on October 28. Odisha has deployed eight ministers to oversee preparedness, shut educational institutions in six vulnerable districts.

item.title: ECI SIR controversy: Why did UP order scrutiny of Form 6, 7 and 8 entered since April 10? What voters should know
item.description: The Uttar Pradesh Chief Election Officer (CEO) ordered scrutiny of all voter forms (Forms 6, 7, and 8) entered by computer assistants since April 10.&nbsp;

item.title: When humanoid robot fell during Kung Fu China demo, losing part of leg - What went wrong? Chinese social media reactions
item.description: Unitree’s newly unveiled H2-X humanoid robot lost part of its leg after a failed side flip during a kung fu demonstration in Hangzhou, China. The mishap drew mixed reactions online, with users debating mechanical design, product safety and the challenges of moving robots

item.title: ‘Set an example’: Employees asked to switch off ACs after 5 PM; here's why Hyderabad water board offices have new rules
item.description: Hyderabad’s water board has ordered offices to cut water and electricity use by at least 20%. Air conditioners must be set to 25°C and switched off after 5 PM. Check other directives.&nbsp;

item.title: LPG cylinder new rules 2026 from Nov 1: How will it impact your household budget and the way you book a refill
item.description: From November 1, LPG users may face updated cylinder prices and stricter enforcement of Aadhaar e-KYC rules. Commercial LPG rates await the monthly OMC announcement, while Delhi’s domestic 14.2-kg cylinder remains ₹942.&nbsp;

item.title: Meet Abijit Ganguly: Stand-up comedian leaves Mumbai after 9 years; more celebs settle from Maximum City; here’s why
item.description: Comedian Abijit Ganguly has moved from Mumbai to Bengaluru after nine years, citing constant construction and a desire for more greenery, space and better surroundings for his young child.&nbsp;

item.title: Rahul Gandhi’s convoy involved in accident: Four cars collide with ambulance on UP’s Purvanchal Expressway — Video
item.description: Rahul Gandhi's convoy involved in collision: Four cars collide with ambulance on UP's Purvanchal Expressway | Video

item.title: Can an English release help Indian films break out beyond the diaspora?
item.description: Indian films so far have made money overseas with a diaspora audience that prefers to watch in the original langugage. Can English dubs expand that business?
